plan.chapterName: Anton, Bivens, and Davis. Calculus, 10th Edition, Figure 14.3.10
plan.contextChunk: This figure is part of a worked example asking to evaluate the polar double integral of sin theta over the region R in the first quadrant outside the circle r = 2 and inside the cardioid r = 2(1 + cos theta). The figure shows both curves in polar coordinates: the circle r = 2 (blue) centered at the origin and the cardioid r = 2(1 + cos theta) (purple), which extends further to the right. The shaded region R (light blue) lies in the first quadrant between theta = 0 and theta = pi/2, bounded on the inside by the circle and on the outside by the cardioid; a red radial line at an intermediate angle shows a representative radial strip. The figure establishes the geometry of the integration region R needed to set up the polar iterated integral with inner limits from r = 2 to r = 2(1 + cos theta) and outer limits from theta = 0 to theta = pi/2.

interactionPlan.concept: A polar double integral over this first-quadrant region is set up by sweeping radial strips whose inner radius is the circle r = 2 and whose outer radius is the cardioid r = 2(1 + cos theta).
elements: horizontal polar axis through the origin labeled theta = 0
vertical axis through the origin labeled theta = pi/2
origin at the intersection of the axes
blue circle r = 2 centered at the origin, labeled r = 2
purple cardioid r = 2(1 + cos theta), labeled r = 2(1 + cos theta)
light blue shaded region R in the first quadrant outside the circle and inside the cardioid
red radial line or radial strip at a representative angle theta inside the shaded region
inner radial boundary segment on the circle r = 2
outer radial boundary segment on the cardioid
intersection point of the circle and cardioid at theta = pi/2
rightmost boundary point of the shaded region along theta = 0
math labels for theta = 0, theta = pi/2, r = 2, and r = 2(1 + cos theta)

interactions.label: Outer polar boundary
interactions.teaches: The formula for the outer polar curve determines where it lies relative to the fixed circle r = 2, where the two boundaries intersect, and therefore the size of the integration region

interactions.label: theta
interactions.teaches: For each angle theta in the first quadrant, the radial slice begins at r = 2 and ends at r = 2(1 + cos theta), so the polar limits are 2 <= r <= 2(1 + cos theta)

demo_steps.title: Identify the two radial bounds
demo_steps.narration: The blue circle is the inner boundary r = 2, while the purple cardioid is the outer boundary r = 2(1 + cos theta). The shaded region is the set of points outside the circle but still inside the cardioid.

demo_steps.title: Start the sweep at theta = 0
demo_steps.narration: At theta = 0, the cardioid has radius 4, so the radial slice runs from r = 2 to r = 4 along the positive x-axis.

demo_steps.title: Sweep through the region
demo_steps.narration: As theta increases, the red radial strip traces the region R. At every angle, the inner endpoint stays on the circle and the outer endpoint stays on the cardioid.

demo_steps.title: End at the intersection angle
demo_steps.narration: At theta = pi/2, the cardioid radius equals 2, so the outer and inner boundaries meet and the radial strip has zero length. This gives the angular limit 0 <= theta <= pi/2.

interactionPlan.keyInsight: The polar integral comes directly from the radial sweep: theta goes from 0 to pi/2, and for each theta the radius runs from the circle r = 2 out to the cardioid r = 2(1 + cos theta).
interactionPlan.reconstructionNotes: Use a clean polar-coordinate style SVG on a white background. Draw black horizontal and vertical axes crossing at the origin, with the horizontal axis extending farther right than left and the vertical axis extending above and below the origin. The circle r = 2 should be a thick blue curve centered at the origin. The cardioid should be a thick purple curve with its cusp at the origin and its widest part extending to the right. Shade only the first-quadrant region between the blue circle and the purple cardioid in translucent light blue. The red radial strip should pivot from the origin; emphasize the actual integration segment between r = 2 and the cardioid while optionally showing a faint guide from the origin. Place labels in large italic math style: r = 2 near the left side of the circle, r = 2(1 + cos theta) above the cardioid, theta = 0 near the positive horizontal axis, and theta = pi/2 near the positive vertical axis.
